subject: Sprint 3 repair of S3-R-01, S3-R-02, S3-R-03 in the governed answer() surface
summary: Each of the three prior High findings was re-derived independently, from corpora I constructed for this review and synced through the real connector into real SQLite, rather than accepted on the delivered fixtures. S3-R-03 is fully repaired and survives five constructed multi-source shapes, backed by a new construction-time invariant that no chunk may be cited by more than one claim. S3-R-01 and S3-R-02 are repaired only for the exact shapes they were reported against: contradiction handling -- both the new conflict signal and the merge refusal, verified separately with conflict detection bypassed -- is keyed to a closed 14-word vocabulary, so out-of-vocabulary and numeric contradictions still produce one SYNTHESIZED claim asserting both sides with zero conflicts, reproduced through the shipped lee-kb ask command; and the evidenced-absence path still replaces a responsive two-source canonical answer when a short same-topic absence sentence ranks first. The sprint invariants (governed composition over retrieve(), resolving citations, distinguishable absence states, INACCESSIBLE never reported as NOT_FOUND, derived confidence, no runtime dependency, no LLM client) all hold under repository-wide checks. One absolute host path remains in a tracked test file.

findings.category: Correctness / conflict detection and claim assembly
findings.problem: Both halves of the S3-R-01 repair -- the new conflict signal and the merge refusal -- are keyed to the same closed 14-word vocabulary (active, approved, blocked, closed, created, denied, disabled, enabled, inactive, never, not, open, optional, required). _value_words_diverge returns False unless BOTH sides contribute a term from that set, so a contradiction expressed outside it reproduces the original S3-R-01 failure exactly: one SYNTHESIZED claim asserting both sides, zero conflicts. Independently constructed and proven (probe A, three corpora, each two same-authority sources written to disk, discovered through the real LocalFilesConnector and projected into real SQLite): 'The release gate for Kestrel is enabled.' vs '... is turned off.' (Jaccard 0.500) yields 1 claim, confidence synthesized, text asserting both, 0 conflicts; 'The export policy for Vega is permitted.' vs '... is forbidden.' (0.600) yields the same; 'The retention window for Lyra is 30 days.' vs '... is 90 days.' (0.667) yields the same. In each case _conflict_signal falls through the value-word check (one side empty), the authority check (equal), and the supersession check (no wording, equal timestamps) and returns None. Numeric divergence -- the commonest contradiction shape in a policy corpus -- is not covered at all, and _subject_terms discards decimals at answer_conflict.py:250, so 30 and 90 are invisible to detection and count as identical subjects for the similarity merge. Both halves fail on exactly the same inputs: with answer.detect_conflicts neutralized, the merged claim is still produced, so improving detection alone would not close it. Reproduced end to end through the shipped CLI: lee-kb sync then lee-kb ask 'What is the state of the release gate for Kestrel?' prints one claim under 'Confidence: synthesized' reading '... is enabled. ... is turned off.', cites both files, and shows no Conflicts section. The in-vocabulary shape the new fixture covers does work (probe A case A1: 2 singly-cited claims, 1 Conflict, and the merge still refused with detection bypassed), so the repair is real but its reach is the fourteen words. This violates the invariant asserted at src/lee_kb/answer.py:23-26 for every contradiction outside them.
findings.proposed_fix: Stop treating contradiction as a lexical-membership test. (1) Invert the merge rule in _assemble_initial_claims: merge only when the two texts' differing meaningful terms are empty or a known synonym set, instead of merging unless a known antonym is seen -- over-conservative merging is always safe, since two unmerged agreeing sources cost only one extra cited claim. (2) Add numeric divergence as an explicit conflict signal: when two same-subject statements share a unit or measure context and carry different numeric literals, emit a Conflict and refuse the merge; drop the blanket isdecimal() discard from _subject_terms so figures participate in subject comparison. (3) Extend benchmark family 5 with three fixtures -- an out-of-vocabulary antonym pair, a numeric contradiction, and a negation-only pair -- each asserting exactly one Conflict and two singly-cited claims.

findings.location: src/lee_kb/answer_absence.py:243 _explicit_absence_evidence (:252-254 top-rank gate, :264 relevance gate); src/lee_kb/answer.py:239-240 and :321 _assemble_evidenced_absence (:341 demotion detail)
findings.problem: The S3-R-02 repair narrows the evidenced-absence short-circuit but keeps its shape: when the gate passes, the whole answer is replaced by that one claim and every other selected evidence item is demoted to evidence_omitted under 'Not part of the explicit statement answering this question.' The two new gates are weak -- the relevance gate is the default 0.25 threshold, so a single shared term suffices for a four-term question, and the top-rank gate is a BM25 ranking accident that short documents win. Independently constructed and proven as a control/treatment A/B (probe B2): asking 'What does the aurora readiness review require?' over two CANONICAL sources that answer it returns 2 DIRECTLY_EVIDENCED claims citing both. Adding one short CANONICAL decision record reading 'The aurora readiness review dossier does not exist.' to the identical corpus makes that record rank first in the governed bundle and collapses the answer to 1 claim, still labelled DIRECTLY_EVIDENCED, with absence None, citing only the dossier note, while both substantive canonical sources are demoted to evidence_omitted. The absence sentence's relevance against the question's four meaningful terms is 0.750, three times the gate. The reader is told confidently and with a citation that a dossier does not exist when they asked what the review requires, with no signal that the real answer was suppressed. Probe B reproduces the prior review's exact construction (an unrelated absence note added to an otherwise identical two-source corpus) and confirms that shape is genuinely fixed -- the substantive claims survive -- so this is the residual class, not a regression.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the evidenced absence an additional claim rather than a replacement: assemble claims from the full selected evidence as normal, then, if _explicit_absence_evidence matches, append its cited statement as one more DIRECTLY_EVIDENCED claim in rank order. That preserves the family-4 guarantee that an explicit 'was never created' is cited rather than silently empty, makes suppression impossible by construction, and removes the need for the top-rank heuristic entirely. If a replacement path is kept, require the absence sentence's subject terms to cover the question's head terms rather than 25% of any terms, and add a regression fixture for 'absence statement about a different aspect of the same topic, ranked first' asserting the substantive claims survive.

findings.problem: A tracked file in a public repository hardcodes an absolute POSIX home path: uri=f"file:///home/lee/{item_id.source_object_id}". This is the class the project deliberately purged from project memory (S2-R-01, S2-R-02, S2-R-12; context.md Environment Notes records that the working-directory path is intentionally not recorded because the repository is public). A repository-wide scan over all 94 tracked files for the whole class -- /home/<user>, /Users/<user>, C:\Users\, /root/, /var/folders/, /private/var/, /mnt/..., /media/..., /opt/..., /srv/..., ~/<a>/<b> -- returns this as the only hit outside code-reviews/; the remaining hits are the documented public config contract ~/.config/lee-kb/config.toml, which is not a host-path leak. Rated High under this step's declared disclosure policy that any leak of the class is at least a High finding. Stated plainly for calibration: it discloses the account name 'lee', already public via the repository owner leebase/lee-kb, the documented author, and the default principal lee@leebase.com in src/lee_kb/main.py; it does not disclose the checkout location, private corpus content, or anything credential-shaped, and it is pre-existing Sprint 1 test code outside the Sprint 3 slice. On impact alone the rating would be Low.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with a neutral synthetic path -- file:///synthetic/{item_id.source_object_id} or a tmp_path-derived URI -- and add the absolute-host-path pattern class to a tools/ disclosure check that scans git ls-files, so the whole repository is checked automatically rather than reviewer-by-reviewer.

findings.problem: _conflict_signal emits a Conflict between statements that do not disagree, because both of its non-supersession signals fire on token overlap alone. Shape A, introduced by the S3-R-01 repair (probe A case A5): two same-authority sources reading 'The Corvus sign-off is required.' and 'The Corvus sign-off is required and approved.' -- which agree, the second merely adding information -- produce one Conflict detailed 'Competing statements about corvus, sign-off use divergent value words.', because _value_words_diverge compares value-word SETS and {required} != {required, approved}. Shape B, pre-existing but now easier to reach (probe B treatment run): three documents where two CANONICAL sources state harbor-readiness requirements and one unrelated DERIVED note reads 'The legacy harbor manifest does not exist.' produce two conflicts, both detailed 'Competing statements about harbor have different declared authority.' The only thing the statements share is the token 'harbor'; neither competes with the other. A reader shown a Conflicts section naming disagreements that do not exist loses the ability to trust the section when it matters, and a machine consumer filtering on conflicts gets false positives. Neither shape is covered by benchmark family 5, whose fixtures all contain genuine contradictions.
findings.proposed_fix: For the value-word branch, require the divergence to be an antonym relationship (or, under the S3-R-10 fix, an actual difference in what the statements assert), not mere set inequality. For the authority branch, require the two statements to be about the same predicate, not merely to share a subject token -- for example, require that they are otherwise near-duplicates, the same condition assembly already uses to consider merging. Add two negative fixtures to family 5: agreeing sources with asymmetric value words, and same-topic cross-authority sources making unrelated statements, each asserting zero conflicts.

findings.problem: The benchmark document states without qualification that S3-R-01, S3-R-02 and S3-R-03 'are repaired, each with a permanent regression fixture', and family 5b's description generalizes to 'Two sources of the same declared authority that directly contradict each other still produce one Conflict and two separate, singly-cited claims.' My probes contradict the generalization: that guarantee holds only when both sides draw from _VALUE_WORDS (S3-R-10), and family 4b's guarantee holds only when the absence sentence is not top-ranked (S3-R-11). The document's recommendation value -- 'Ready after specific follow-up' -- is inside the declared vocabulary and happens to match my own conclusion, but the text justifies it with a completeness claim that is not true, and its list of what remains open contains no correctness defect at all ('None of these are correctness defects in the repaired slice'). A reader using this document to decide whether to release would be materially misled. Everything else in it that I could re-derive reproduces exactly: the Confidence Distribution (probe E -- 9 DIRECTLY_EVIDENCED plus 1 SYNTHESIZED = 10 claims over the five family-7 questions, 0 unresolved citations, so S3-R-06 is genuinely closed), the same-authority Conflict Example (probe E -- detail string, newer=NEITHER, more_authoritative=NEITHER, no winner attribute), and the 15 collected benchmark items.
findings.proposed_fix: Qualify both fixture descriptions to the shape actually guaranteed ('two sources whose divergence is expressed with a recognized value-word pair'; 'an absence-shaped sentence that is not the top-ranked chunk'), and move S3-R-10 and S3-R-11 into the Recommendation's open list as correctness defects, above the honest-reporting and documentation items. Keep the recommendation value; change what it is gated on.

governed_surface_exclusivity.justification: Clean. Probe D1: the complete set of repository calls during answer() is search (from lee_kb.retrieval) then record_receipt x2 (from lee_kb.governance), identical to the sequence retrieve() alone produces on the same inputs, with no call originating in any lee_kb.answer* module. Neutralizing answer.retrieve makes answer() raise rather than fall back, so there is no alternate evidence path. answer() composes strictly over governance.retrieve().

citations_and_receipt_closure.justification: Clean. Probe D2: over four questions, 5 claims, 0 uncited claims and 0 unresolved citations -- every item_id and chunk_id resolves to a real item and chunk in the projection -- and receipt_ids covers exactly evidence_used union evidence_omitted on all four. Probe E: 0 unresolved citations over the twelve-document benchmark corpus. Every substantive claim carries a resolving citation.

absence_states.justification: The three absence states remain distinguishable and an inaccessible result is never reported as NOT_FOUND (probe D3: withheld corpus -> INACCESSIBLE with withheld_count 1 and UNKNOWN confidence, asserted not NOT_FOUND; silence -> NOT_FOUND; unsynchronized project -> UNKNOWN; resolution failure -> UNKNOWN; each with a distinct detail). The residual defect is the evidenced-absence path replacing, rather than joining, a responsive answer.

conflict_detection_and_claim_assembly.justification: Correct for the in-vocabulary contradiction shape the new fixture covers, including the merge refusal proven with conflict detection bypassed; incorrect for out-of-vocabulary and numeric contradictions, and over-triggering on statements that do not disagree.

conflict_reconciliation.justification: Clean. Probe C over five constructed multi-source shapes: max 1 claim per chunk in every case, no merged claim resurrected asserting both sides, no crash. Reinforced by the new construction-time invariant at answer_contracts.py:548 that a chunk may be cited by at most one claim. S3-R-03 fully repaired.

confidence_model.justification: Clean. Probe D4: answer()'s signature contains no confidence parameter, so a caller cannot assert one; the same question yields directly_evidenced over a single source and synthesized over two independent sources. Confidence is derived from evidence shape.
